premises: Constituent elements have different thermal expansion coefficients, generating local thermal stresses during high-temperature exposure and cooling.
These thermal stresses drive localized compositional segregation and nano-scale lattice distortions or fine precipitates.
Such microstructural changes modify dislocation motion and elastic response, unifying creep, cold-rolling hardness, elastic moduli, and age-hardening behavior.
A compositional variant with reduced thermal expansion mismatch will show diminished segregation, lattice strain, and altered mechanical properties.
The effects are prominent only at high temperatures (≥600 °C aging, ~1250 °C creep) and not at room temperature.
